primary_diagnosis: Unstable Angina Pectoris

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Retrosternal chest discomfort on minimal exertion, mild peripheral edema.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Administered Aspirin 150mg daily, Atorvastatin 40mg nightly.

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Persistent intermittent angina. Renal markers stable.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Initiated Metoprolol succinate 25mg OD (ACE-inhibitors withheld due to borderline eGFR).

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Angina resolved, exertional tolerance restored without orthopnea.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Maintained dual antianginal regimen, scheduled outpatient cardiorenal follow-up.

adverse_or_contraindicated_drugs: Lisinopril (withheld due to risk of hyperkalemia/acute kidney injury)
treatment_outcome.clinical_notes_raw: Patient presented with retrosternal chest pain on a background of DKD and long-standing hypertension. Renin-angiotensin blockade was contraindicated due to baseline creatinine elevation of 1.8 mg/dL and eGFR 38 mL/min. Patient stabilized well on low-dose cardioselective beta-blocker without worsening renal parameters.

primary_diagnosis: Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction (HFrEF NYHA III)

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, bilateral pedal pitting edema (grade 3), bibasilar rales.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: IV Furosemide 40mg BID, Apixaban 2.5mg BID dose-adjusted for age and creatinine.

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Significant diuresis (net -2.4L), breathing easier in supine position.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Transitioned to oral Torsemide 20mg OD, added Sacubitril/Valsartan 24/26mg BID with close potassium monitoring.

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Euvolemic, trace ankle edema, ambulatory on ward without breathlessness.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Added Empagliflozin 10mg daily for cardiorenal protection.

adverse_or_contraindicated_drugs: Spironolactone (deferred due to borderline potassium 5.2 mEq/L and eGFR 32)
treatment_outcome.clinical_notes_raw: Severe decompensated heart failure with concomitant atrial fibrillation and renal impairment. Successful diuresis achieved with loop diuretics. Neurohormonal blockade initiated cautiously at lowest tier of ARNI while Spironolactone was deferred to prevent fatal hyperkalemia.

primary_diagnosis: Non-ST Elevation Myocardial Infarction (NSTEMI)

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Severe crushing substernal chest pressure radiating to left jaw, diaphoresis. Troponin-I 4.8 ng/mL.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Loading dose Aspirin 300mg, Ticagrelor 180mg, Heparin bolus plus infusion, transfer to cath lab.

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Post-PCI to mid-LAD drug-eluting stent. No recurrence of chest pain. Radial puncture site dry.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Aspirin 81mg daily, Ticagrelor 90mg BID, Rosuvastatin 40mg nightly, Bisoprolol 5mg daily.

adverse_or_contraindicated_drugs: NSAIDs (strictly prohibited post-ACS)
treatment_outcome.clinical_notes_raw: Acute coronary syndrome with single vessel disease treated by primary stenting. Prescribed guideline-directed medical therapy consisting of dual antiplatelet therapy for 12 months with high-intensity statin and cardioselective beta blockade.

primary_diagnosis: Persistent Atrial Fibrillation with Rapid Ventricular Response

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Palpitations, lightheadedness, presyncope upon standing.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: IV Diltiazem drip titrated to rate < 100 bpm, initiated Edoxaban 30mg OD.

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Resting ventricular rate controlled at 74 bpm. Lightheadedness completely resolved.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Oral Diltiazem CD 180mg daily, continued Edoxaban 30mg OD adjusted for renal clearance.

adverse_or_contraindicated_drugs: Amiodarone (documented allergy - pulmonary toxicity risk)
Digoxin (withheld due to fall risk)
treatment_outcome.clinical_notes_raw: Elderly patient with fast AF rate managed via non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker rather than beta-blockers due to reactive airway tendency. Anticoagulation achieved with renal-adjusted DOAC.

primary_diagnosis: Refractory Hypertension and Hypertensive Urgency

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Occipital throbbing headache, blurred vision, epistaxis.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Oral Labetalol 200mg stat, Amlodipine 10mg OD, Telmisartan 80mg OD.

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Headache improved, blood pressure trending down gradually.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Added Chlorthalidone 12.5mg daily to triple antihypertensive regimen.

adverse_or_contraindicated_drugs: Short-acting sublingual Nifedipine (contraindicated due to risk of stroke/MI)
treatment_outcome.clinical_notes_raw: Hypertensive crisis managed without rapid precipitous drops in arterial pressure. Combination therapy using CCB, ARB, and thiazide-like diuretic restored controlled hemodynamics.

primary_diagnosis: Chronic Stable Angina with Multi-vessel Disease

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: CCS Class III exertional angina, heavy chest tightening after 50 meters walk.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Clopidogrel 75mg OD (aspirin substitute), Isosorbide Mononitrate 30mg OD, Ranolazine 500mg BID.

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Noticeable improvement in walking tolerance, no chest tightness at normal pace.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Maintained Ranolazine and nitrate regimen, avoided thiazides to prevent gout flare.

adverse_or_contraindicated_drugs: Aspirin (severe aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease)
Hydrochlorothiazide (exacerbates hyperuricemia)
treatment_outcome.clinical_notes_raw: Stable coronary disease in aspirin-intolerant diabetic with moderate renal decline. Ranolazine offered antianginal efficacy without lowering heart rate or blood pressure.

primary_diagnosis: Dilated Cardiomyopathy with Frequent Premature Ventricular Complexes

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Skipped beats, chest fluttering, fatigue, LVEF 38%.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Initiated Carvedilol 6.25mg BID, Lisinopril 5mg daily, Dapagliflozin 10mg daily.

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Holter monitor shows PVC burden reduced from 14% to 2.1%. Fatigue improved.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Uptitrated Carvedilol to 12.5mg BID.

adverse_or_contraindicated_drugs: Class Ic antiarrhythmics (Flecainide contraindicated in structural heart disease)
treatment_outcome.clinical_notes_raw: Cardiomyopathy with non-sustained ventricular ectopic activity responsive to combined alpha/beta antagonism and SGLT2 inhibition.

primary_diagnosis: Diabetic Kidney Disease Stage 4 with Severe Proteinuria

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Foamy urine, bilateral lower limb edema (+2), generalized sluggishness.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (uACR) 1420 mg/g. Initiated Finerenone 10mg daily, Torsemide 10mg daily.

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Edema decreased, potassium monitored at 4.8 mEq/L (safe threshold).
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Maintained Finerenone, withheld SGLT2i initiation as eGFR < 25 mL/min baseline per older local protocol.

adverse_or_contraindicated_drugs: High dose Spironolactone (hyperkalemia danger in eGFR < 30)
Metformin (contraindicated in eGFR < 30)
treatment_outcome.clinical_notes_raw: Advanced diabetic nephropathy with nephrotic-range microalbuminuria. Non-steroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist Finerenone introduced with tight serum potassium checks, successfully avoiding RAAS-induced hyperkalemic episodes.

primary_diagnosis: Primary Membranous Nephropathy with Nephrotic Syndrome

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Severe anasarca, facial puffiness, 24-hr urine protein 6.8 grams. Anti-PLA2R positive.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Started Modified Ponticelli protocol: IV Methylprednisolone pulse followed by oral Prednisone and Cyclophosphamide.

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Gradual reduction in ascites and peripheral swelling. Urine protein decreased to 2.9 g/24h.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Initiated prophylactic Enoxaparin 40mg OD due to serum albumin < 2.0 g/dL thrombotic risk.

adverse_or_contraindicated_drugs: NSAIDs (risk of acute interstitial nephritis and renal shutdown)
treatment_outcome.clinical_notes_raw: Anti-PLA2R positive membranous nephropathy presenting with profound hypoalbuminemia. Remission induction accomplished with cyclic corticosteroid and alkylating agent along with prophylactic anticoagulation.

primary_diagnosis: Acute Kidney Injury on Chronic Kidney Disease Stage 3

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Oliguria following gastroenteritis and self-administration of OTC Ibuprofen. Creatinine spike to 4.2 mg/dL.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Stopped Ibuprofen immediately, aggressive IV volume resuscitation with 0.9% Normal Saline 100 mL/hr.

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Urine output normalized to 1800 mL/24h. Electrolytes stabilized.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Discontinued IV fluids, resumed oral hydration, educated patient on nephrotoxic drug avoidance.

adverse_or_contraindicated_drugs: Ibuprofen / NSAIDs (precipitating nephrotoxic agent)
Aminoglycosides
treatment_outcome.clinical_notes_raw: Hemodynamically mediated acute kidney injury precipitated by volume depletion compounded by non-steroidal anti-inflammatory ingestion. Successfully reversed with prompt fluid expansion.

primary_diagnosis: Lupus Nephritis Class IV (Diffuse Proliferative)

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Active urinary sediment with RBC casts, malar rash, arthralgias. Low complement C3/C4.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Mycophenolate Mofetil (MMF) 1g BID, Hydroxychloroquine 200mg OD, high-dose oral Prednisolone.

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: RBC casts cleared from urine, joint pain subsided, complement levels rising.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Continued MMF maintenance, initiated steroid taper.

adverse_or_contraindicated_drugs: Live vaccines (contraindicated under immunosuppression)
treatment_outcome.clinical_notes_raw: Active lupus nephritis confirmed on renal biopsy. Standard induction with MMF and corticosteroids produced prompt clinical response and stabilization of glomerular filtration.

primary_diagnosis: Hypertensive Nephrosclerosis with Refractory Hyperkalemia

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Muscle weakness, ECG peaked T-waves. Potassium level 6.1 mEq/L.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: IV Calcium Gluconate 1g stat, Insulin-Dextrose infusion, Patiromer 8.4g daily.

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Muscle power restored, ECG normalized. Potassium lowered to 4.7 mEq/L.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Maintained daily Patiromer binder, adjusted diet to low potassium intake.

adverse_or_contraindicated_drugs: Enalapril (severe prior angioedema)
Potassium-sparing diuretics
treatment_outcome.clinical_notes_raw: Chronic hypertensive nephropathy complicated by hyperkalemic emergency. Controlled through oral non-absorbed potassium binder Patiromer without needing acute hemodialysis.

primary_diagnosis: ADPKD (Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease)

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Bilateral flank fullness, microscopic hematuria, early satiety.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Initiated Tolvaptan 45mg/15mg split dose, emphasized vigorous oral hydration (>3.5 L/day).

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Well-tolerated aquaresis, flank discomfort stable, hepatic panel normal.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Continued monthly transaminase monitoring per REMS requirement.

adverse_or_contraindicated_drugs: Thiazide diuretics (worsens volume contraction with vasopressin antagonist)
treatment_outcome.clinical_notes_raw: Rapidly progressing ADPKD treated with V2-receptor antagonist to retard cyst growth and GFR decline rate. Rigorous liver function and sodium monitoring maintained.

primary_diagnosis: CKD Mineral and Bone Disorder (CKD-MBD) with Secondary Hyperparathyroidism

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Bone aches, pruritus, intact PTH 480 pg/mL, Phosphate 6.4 mg/dL.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Sevelamer Carbonate 800mg TID with meals, Calcitriol 0.25 mcg daily.

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Pruritus resolved, phosphate dropped to 4.6 mg/dL, PTH reduced to 210 pg/mL.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Continued non-calcium phosphate binder to prevent vascular calcification.

adverse_or_contraindicated_drugs: Calcium acetate in high doses (risk of severe adynamic bone disease)
treatment_outcome.clinical_notes_raw: Severe secondary hyperparathyroidism in pre-dialysis renal disease. Regulated successfully with non-calcium phosphate binding polymer and active vitamin D analogue.

primary_diagnosis: Uncontrolled Type-2 Diabetes Mellitus with Metabolic Syndrome

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Polydipsia, polyuria, fasting blood glucose 240 mg/dL, HbA1c 10.4%.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Initiated Semaglutide 0.25mg SC weekly (uptitration schedule), Metformin ER 1000mg BID.

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Appetite noticeably curbed, fasting glucose reduced to 138 mg/dL. Mild nausea on day 2-3.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Uptitrated Semaglutide to 0.5mg weekly per protocol.

adverse_or_contraindicated_drugs: Sulfonylureas (Glimepiride avoided due to hypoglycemia risk)
treatment_outcome.clinical_notes_raw: Significant glycemic dysregulation with elevated body mass index. GLP-1 receptor agonist and biguanide therapy lowered glucose burden without triggering hypoglycemia or weight gain.

primary_diagnosis: Graves' Disease with Moderate Thyrotoxicosis

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Heat intolerance, fine hand tremors, weight loss of 6kg over 4 weeks. Free T4 3.8 ng/dL, TSH < 0.01.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Methimazole 20mg daily, Diltiazem 60mg TID (beta-blocker avoided due to active asthma).

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Palpitations settled, resting heart rate controlled to 76 bpm. Tremors diminished.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Tapered Diltiazem, maintained Methimazole 20mg with scheduled CBC and liver panel check.

adverse_or_contraindicated_drugs: Propranolol (contraindicated due to bronchial asthma history)
Propylthiouracil (hepatotoxicity risk in non-pregnant state)
treatment_outcome.clinical_notes_raw: Hyperthyroid state in asthmatic patient successfully addressed with thionamide and rate control achieved via calcium channel blockade avoiding bronchospastic complications.

primary_diagnosis: Type-2 Diabetes with Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Burning sensation and tingling in bilateral soles disrupting sleep. Fasting blood sugar 182 mg/dL.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Initiated Duloxetine 30mg nightly, increased to 60mg after 1 week. Started Linagliptin 5mg OD.

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Neuropathic pain decreased by 70%, sleeping through the night. Blood glucose down to 132 mg/dL.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Maintained Duloxetine 60mg OD, DPP-4 inhibitor Linagliptin required no renal adjustment.

adverse_or_contraindicated_drugs: Pregabalin (avoided due to peripheral edema tendency and cognitive fog)
treatment_outcome.clinical_notes_raw: Painful diabetic neuropathy managed with SNRI duloxetine. Glycemic control enhanced with Linagliptin which possesses hepatic excretion and requires no renal dose modifications.

primary_diagnosis: Severe Mixed Hyperlipidemia with Hypertriglyceridemia-Induced Pancreatitis Risk

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Eruptive xanthomas on extensor surfaces, triglycerides 980 mg/dL, LDL-C 160 mg/dL.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Started Fenofibrate 145mg daily, Icosapent ethyl 2g BID, strict fat-restricted diet.

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: No abdominal pain, xanthomas regressing. Triglycerides reduced to 340 mg/dL.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Added Atorvastatin 20mg daily with cautious observation of muscle enzymes.

adverse_or_contraindicated_drugs: Gemfibrozil (contraindicated with statins due to rhabdomyolysis risk)
treatment_outcome.clinical_notes_raw: Severe hypertriglyceridemia nearing acute pancreatitis threshold. Fibrate and purified EPA therapy achieved rapid lipid lowering without muscular toxicity.

primary_diagnosis: Primary Adrenal Insufficiency (Addison's Disease)

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Extreme fatigue, orthostatic dizziness, hyperpigmentation of palmar creases. Morning cortisol 1.8 mcg/dL.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Hydrocortisone 15mg morning / 5mg afternoon, Fludrocortisone 0.1mg OD.

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Energy levels normalized, standing blood pressure stabilized, salt craving resolved.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Patient educated on emergency sick-day rules and steroid alert bracelet provided.

adverse_or_contraindicated_drugs: Abrupt steroid discontinuation (life-threatening adrenal crisis)
treatment_outcome.clinical_notes_raw: Autoimmune polyglandular syndrome component with chronic hypocortisolemia. Complete symptomatic recovery achieved with physiological glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid replacement.

primary_diagnosis: Severe Osteoporosis with Lumbar Compression Fracture

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Lower back pain following mild bending, DXA T-score -3.4 at lumbar spine.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Denosumab 60mg SC injection, Calcium carbonate 500mg + Cholecalciferol 1000 IU daily.

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Back pain well controlled, no gastrointestinal symptoms, serum calcium stable at 9.4 mg/dL.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Scheduled 6-month repeat Denosumab; strict instructions never to delay doses.

adverse_or_contraindicated_drugs: Oral Bisphosphonates (contraindicated due to active severe erosive esophagitis)
treatment_outcome.clinical_notes_raw: Severe postmenopausal osteoporosis in patient with active upper GI erosions. RANKL inhibitor Denosumab provided effective bone mineral preservation without gastrointestinal intolerance.
